A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RUT auditing work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained content across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Monte Carlo experiments on model substitutions, score-function comparisons, fine-tuning experiments and audits of commercial API endpoints.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds quantization evaluations on math and coding queries and experiments detecting decoding-parameter mismatches.

M1.justification: RUT retains the same reference sampling, log-rank scoring, randomized empirical ranks and Cramer–von Mises rejection procedure. Clarified score descriptions and the new AUROC pseudocode document the existing procedure rather than establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Section 5.6 adds actual evaluation on BigCodeBench programming queries and MATH problems, substantially extending evaluation beyond WildChat conversational queries. Existing WildChat, Alpaca and BeaverTails coverage is retained.

E2.justification: MMD and the log-rank-based KS test remain the evaluated comparators, including in the new experiments. The other methods discussed in Table 1 remain contextual comparisons rather than newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix B.6 introduces a controlled decoding sweep: temperatures 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0 crossed with top-p values 0.5, 0.75, 0.9 and 1.0, against reference settings (0.5, 1.0). Previously specified query budgets, generation limits, metrics and fine-tuning settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.6 and Figure 5 add a focused sensitivity study asking whether decoding-parameter deviations are detectable across two models and two datasets. The existing score-selection analysis, fine-tuning checkpoint comparisons and whitespace-mismatch case study are retained.

E5.justification: v4 introduces 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for AUCs in Tables 2–3 and 95% Wilson confidence bands for statistical-power curves. Both versions already specify 500 Monte Carlo trials; the revision establishes new uncertainty reporting, not an increase in trial counts.

E6.justification: v4 adds domain-comparison and decoding-mismatch results in Table 3, Figure 5 and Appendix B.5. Several retained B.3 curves also change: Llama/BeaverTails epoch-5 KS power at substitution rate 0.2 changes from approximately 0.63 to 0.24. Original main-text point estimates remain unchanged, and B.5 adds WildChat curves that differ substantially from the retained B.1 curves without explaining the difference.

T1.justification: New Appendix C introduces a Zipf/Zeta token-rank assumption, reparameterization and reordering attack models, two lemmas and two sample-complexity theorems with proofs. This substantially extends the earlier randomized-rank uniformity argument without changing the proposed testing procedure.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction expand the stated empirical contribution to validation across diverse query domains. The central claims of a query-efficient, natural-query auditing test with strong substitution-detection power remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: The limitations replace the earlier emphasis on detecting cross-prompt correlations with a specific knowledgeable adversary that reroutes prompts expected to produce atypical log-ranks. v4 also interprets the new results as supporting domain generality and the usefulness of detecting decoding anomalies. The local-reference-model restriction remains.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-release statement and repository link, AUROC evaluation pseudocode in Appendix A.1, and more explicit score-aggregation descriptions. The previously disclosed hardware, inference budgets and fine-tuning hyperparameters remain. Repository contents cannot be assessed from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion newly emphasizes that fingerprinting seeks stability under deployment changes, whereas auditing seeks sensitivity to them. References for MATH, BigCodeBench, nucleus sampling and Zipf's law are added; the main auditing comparisons and positioning remain.

P1.justification: Targeted edits clarify reference-model access, shorten experimental descriptions, rewrite limitations and remove the visible editorial comment in Section 4.1. Appendix A gains separate algorithm and distribution subsections. The main narrative and section progression remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds a domain-comparison table, decoding heatmaps and an algorithm box, expands tables to display confidence intervals, and redraws power curves with uncertainty bands instead of area fills. Existing displays are also relocated and reformatted within the conference layout.

improvement.justification: v4 improves coverage, uncertainty reporting and reproducibility documentation. However, new B.5 WildChat curves disagree with retained B.1 results: Gemma-4bit RUT power at full substitution is about 0.29 versus 0.882. Table 3 supports six, not the claimed seven, wins among the eight emphasized cases. Theorem C.2 also claims constant sample complexity as the Zipf exponent approaches 1, although its swap moves vanishing probability mass. These new consistency and validity concerns prevent a reliable net-quality judgment despite useful empirical additions.
